title: Statistics & Methodology: Reporting & Probability
welcome_lead: Effect sizes, the APA report and the probability behind it all.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology reporting: peer review, APA format, levels of measurement.
final_note: A finding only counts if others can replicate it.

walkthroughs.body_html: Peer review: independent experts critique a paper before publication, checking method, statistics, originality. Reduces fraud and error. Critics note publication bias — significant results are 3x more likely to be published than null results (Sterling 1959).

Nominal: categories with no order. Ordinal: ranked but intervals unequal. Interval: equal intervals, no absolute zero. Ratio: equal intervals with absolute zero (height, time). Level of measurement determines which statistical test you can use.

Modern reporting includes effect size: small d = 0.2, medium d = 0.5, large d = 0.8 (Cohen 1988). The reproducibility project (Open Science Collaboration 2015) found only 36% of psychology studies replicated — fueling the replication crisis.
